newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch guilder somewhat stronger versus German mark.
newsitem.headline: Dutch guilder somewhat stronger versus German mark.

text.p: The Dutch guilder strengthened slightly versus the German mark on Tuesday after the Dutch central bank raised interest rates on Monday in an attempt to block a further weakening of the guilder.

Dealers said the guilder was likely to remain near current levels for the time being, some commenting that the Dutch currency had not really weakened but was just not quite as strong as it used to be compared with the mark.
The guilder was trading at 112.55 per 100 marks versus 112.63 on Monday.
"It was an exaggeration to say that the guilder was weak," said one. "The guilder is hard as rock," he added.
The dealer said the guilder had consistently traded well below the central rate of 112.673 per 100 marks in recent years, so there was no reason to worry about the Dutch currency.

On Monday the Dutch central bank raised the secured loans rate, which sets the floor for money rates, by 50 basis points to 2.50 percent. It also raised the special advances rate by 20 basis points to 2.90 percent.
"The market is calming down after the rate rises and money market rates are likely to stay near the current level now.
Money market rates rose fractionally this morning as a result of yesterday's interest rate hike.
Call money rates rose to 3.00 percent bid from 2.93 percent on Monday and three-month deposits added two basis points to 3.14 percent bid.

Dealers said there had been substantial interest in Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) this morning as the Dutch Ministry of Finance had raised the rates for its April, May and December DTCs -- short-term borrowing programmes of the Dutch government.
The April DTC programme was set at 3.12 percent, the May programme at 3.14 percent and the December programme at 3.27.
Later in the day the rates on DTCs slipped by one or two basis points.
"This probably means that the Finance Ministry's Agency has taken in a reasonable amount of money," said one dealer.
